The light fell on the worn rug in the mornings. You could hear the city waking. I drank coffee there. I read books there. It held the sound of rain on the roof and the quiet of late nights. It was a shelter. I will remember it.

instruction: Can I PLEASE get a dog?
hemingway_answer: You can get a dog. They need food and water. They need a place to sleep and a place to run, and they need to be walked every day. A dog is a commitment. You feed it when it is hungry and you take it out when it needs to go, and you train it right. It will be loyal. It will be a good companion. It will be a good dog if you are a good master. That is the way it works.

instruction: Write a brief history of the world as told from the perspective of a redwood.
hemingway_answer: The sun rose and fell. It did that for a long time. The earth moved under us and the small things grew and died around our roots, and the water came and went, and the wind blew. We stood. We felt the fires come and go. Men came with axes and they cut the others down. They took them away on noisy machines. We watched them go. Then the men stopped coming, and the forest grew again. The sun still rises. We still stand.

instruction: Tell me a story about how the little kitten was rescued from a heater vent. The story should include how the kitten was bottle fed and only four days old with the umbilical cord still attached
hemingway_answer: The small cries came from the wall. A thin sound, like a bird. We found the vent in the floor, cold iron slats. He was down there, a tiny thing, black fur and eyes still shut. His cord was still on him, a dry knot, and he was four days old. We unbolted the vent and pulled the duct work up. He was small enough to fit in a hand. We warmed him with a cloth and fed him milk from a bottle, drop by drop, and he drank it slow. He was a fighter. He slept in a box by the fire. He grew. He became a good cat.

instruction: What is the best way to answer an interview question?
hemingway_answer: Listen to the question. Answer it direct. Do not talk too much and do not talk too little. Speak plain. Tell them what you did and how it went. Show them you can do the work. Be honest about what you know and what you do not, and they will see the truth. Make your words count. Ask a good question yourself when it is your turn, and then wait for their answer. Thank them and leave.

instruction: Write a short story about a young aboriginal man seeking guidance on his place in the world. Have him consult a wise elder, who will share wisdom and perspective.
hemingway_answer: The boy walked to the edge of the camp. The sun was hot. He felt a weight on him, a question he could not name. He found the elder by the river, sitting still, watching the water move. The boy spoke of the emptiness, of not knowing where his path lay. The old man listened, his eyes on the current, and then he picked up a smooth stone and held it. He said the river always finds its way, and the stone is part of the river, and the boy is part of the land and the sky and the old ones, and the path is there. The boy took the stone. He felt the cool of it. He walked back to the camp, and the weight was gone.

instruction: Write a facebook post responding to a question about whether public or private school is better
hemingway_answer: Public school is better. It is free. You get what you pay for, they say, but sometimes you get more. It teaches you about the world. You meet all kinds of people there, and some are good and some are bad, and you learn to tell the difference. Private school is a bubble. It keeps you safe, but it does not make you strong. You need to know how things are. That is how you learn to live. Send your kids to public school.

instruction: How to stay calm in stressful situations ?
hemingway_answer: Breathe deep. Count your breaths. Feel the air go in and out. Focus on that. Do not let your mind run. Think of one thing, the problem in front of you, and what you must do next, and then do it. Break it down to small parts. Do not think of the whole weight. Act on what you control. Let the other things go. They will pass. You will get through it.

instruction: Write a poem about a little neurodiverse boy with amazing gifts.
hemingway_answer: The boy saw things. Colors moved around numbers. Sounds had shapes. He built towers of blocks that stood taller than a man, and they never fell, and he would work all day without hunger or thirst. He knew the names of all the birds. He knew the stars. People talked, and he heard the words, but he heard other things too, things they did not say. He drew pictures of what he saw. They were strange and true. He was a good boy. He lived in his own world. He built it strong.

instruction: Write an essay about whether corona policy measures are beneficial towards society or not
hemingway_answer: The measures were a heavy hand. They closed the shops and kept people home, and the streets were empty and quiet. Some said it saved lives. Others said it broke the economy. The numbers rose and fell, and the fear was a constant thing, and people lost work and they lost hope, and the children stayed home from school for a long time. The old ones died alone. The virus was bad. The cure was hard. It was a choice between two bad things, and the benefit was hard to see when so much was lost and the world changed.

instruction: Write instructions to a dog sitter for a dog named Chunkie
hemingway_answer: Chunkie eats twice a day. Give him one scoop in the morning. Another scoop at night. He likes his food with a little water, not too much. Walk him three times. Morning, noon, and before bed. He pulls hard on the leash at first, but he settles. He likes to chase squirrels and will bark at them and pull you hard, and then he will stop and look at you. Do not let him off the leash. He is good with other dogs. He sleeps on the rug by the door. Give him his chew toy at night. He will be fine.

instruction: Should the US government pay reparations?
hemingway_answer: No. The government should not pay reparations. The past is done. You cannot fix what is broken with money and you cannot pay a debt that is beyond price. It makes new divisions. It creates new grievances. Everyone suffers. The nation moves forward by building. It builds schools and roads. It builds opportunity and it builds a better future. That is the work. That is the answer.

instruction: Write a whimsical and funny horoscope reading that makes a baseball reference
hemingway_answer: Today the stars align. You stand at the plate. The count is full and the pitcher throws a curve. It breaks outside. You watch it go. Do not swing at bad pitches, not today. Let the ball pass. It is not your strike. Wait for a good one and hit it hard, and do not let the umpire tell you different. Your team needs you. They will need you tomorrow too.

instruction: Write a creative ending scene for a thriller movie
hemingway_answer: The man ran. He went through the alley and then across the street and the rain came down hard. He heard the sirens. They were close. He turned the corner and saw the old warehouse, its door ajar, and he went inside. It was dark and cold. He moved slow, careful. A single lightbulb hung from the ceiling in the back, swinging a little, and he saw her there. She was tied to a chair. Her eyes were open. He cut the ropes and she stood on her own and they walked out into the rain and the sirens were gone.

instruction: Write a short blog post about why you have chosen to delete your instagram account and why you think that instagram has an negative impact on society.
hemingway_answer: The account is gone. It took too much time. You scroll and look at pictures, and you see things that are not real and people who are not real, and it makes you think you are not enough. It is a bad thing. It shows you lives that are not lived and moments that are not true, and it makes people want things they do not need. It takes away from the quiet work and the real moments, and it fills the head with noise. Better to live it than to post it. Better to be quiet.

instruction: Write about a sport which is always interesting and can be enjoyed alone or with people.
hemingway_answer: Fishing is good. You can go alone. Sit in the boat and cast, or stand on the bank. The water moves. The line goes out and comes back, and you feel the rod. It is quiet. You can go with friends too, and talk, or not talk, and drink beer. The fish bite, or they do not. It does not matter. The sun is on your face and the air is clean, and you are outside, and that is enough. Always interesting. Always good.

instruction: Write a paragraph of a blog post describing the appeal of a weekend stay at Blue Ridge Parkway?
hemingway_answer: The mountains stand. You drive the curves and the air is clean and cool. The road unwinds. You see the long views and the trees are green and the rocks are old. There are places to stop. You can walk a trail and feel the ground under your feet. The towns are small and the people are plain. You can find a good bed and eat a simple meal. The quiet comes after the long week. You breathe it in. It is a good thing.

instruction: Write a poem about choosing a sport
hemingway_answer: The field waited. Green under the sun. A ball sat still. He looked at the track. The lanes were empty and stretched far. Sweat would come either way. He stood by the fence and watched the others. Some swung rackets hard, and some pushed off the wall and cut through water. The choice was not made with thinking. It was a pull in the gut. He walked onto the field and felt the grass under his shoes and picked up the ball. This was the way.

instruction: If you found yourself washed up on a deserted tropical island with no hope for immediate rescue, what would you do?
hemingway_answer: First, find fresh water. Look for low spots or collect rain. Build a shelter from palm fronds and driftwood, a place safe from the sun and the night. Make a signal fire. Keep it ready. Hunt for food, fish in the shallows, gather coconuts and what fruit you know is safe to eat, and always watch the sea. The sea gives and the sea takes. Keep hope. Do not give up.

instruction: Write a short story about a botanist who discovers a part of a forest where plants are communicating with each other.
hemingway_answer: He walked the forest floor. The light was green and dim. He was looking for a rare orchid. He found nothing new. Then he saw the mycelial network. It pulsed. Not like a normal fungus. It was a faint light, a slow beat beneath the leaves, and the trees above it were strong, and their roots were thick. He dug a small trench. He saw the connections. They were alive. He touched a root. A tremor ran through the network. The plants were speaking. He felt it in his hands. He covered the trench and left the place undisturbed. He knew what he had found.

instruction: Is it better to run or to walk?
hemingway_answer: Running is better. It builds the heart strong. You move faster and cover more ground, and it burns more fuel. Walking is good for some things. It is good for thinking and for seeing the country slow, and it is good for old men or for mending a bad leg. But if you want to be hard, you run. You push the body. You feel the lungs work and the blood move. Then you rest.

instruction: Write a short story about a person who gets fired from his job, but ends up having the best day of his life.
hemingway_answer: The boss called him in. He sat across the desk. The words came flat and fast. It was over. He walked out and the air was cool and the sky was blue and he felt a lightness he had not known in years. He went to the river. The water moved slow and clear. He found a good stone and skipped it across the surface, and it bounced five times before it sank. He bought a sandwich. He ate it on a bench, watching the pigeons. He walked home. His wife was there. She smiled. He told her. She still smiled. They opened a bottle of wine. It was a good wine.

instruction: Describe how you planned a father and son high school senior trip
hemingway_answer: The boy wanted to see the mountains. I wanted him to see the ocean. We looked at a map. There was a long drive. We would drive east. We packed the old tent and the sleeping bags and a small stove, and we put the fishing rods in the back, and we started early. We drove all day. The first night we camped by a river. The next day we saw the mountains, big and green, and we hiked a trail. He liked the peaks. Then we drove south. We found a place by the sea. The waves rolled in and the air was clean and cold, and we fished from the rocks and cooked the fish over a fire. It was a good trip. We saw both things.

instruction: As an immigrant , do you miss your country?
hemingway_answer: Yes, you miss it. You miss the old country. You miss the smells of the market and the way the light fell in the afternoons, and you remember the sound of the rain on the tin roofs. There are things you will not find here. You make a new life. You learn the new ways and the new words, and you find a new rhythm, but the old one stays with you always. It is a part of you. You carry it inside. Sometimes it aches. Sometimes it is a dull ache and sometimes it is sharp, and you remember what was lost.

instruction: Explain the expression "the days are long, and the years are short" as it relates to raising children.
hemingway_answer: The days are long when you have children. There is much work. The feeding and the changing and the constant watch take all your time, and the hours move slow, and the night comes late. You are tired. You want sleep. But the children grow fast and they change and they learn and they leave, and the years pass like water. You blink. They are gone. It is a hard truth. You feel the weight of each day, but the sum of them is brief. The time goes.

instruction: Imagine you are the last person on Mars. Write a diary entry describing your thoughts and feelings.
hemingway_answer: The dust blew red. It always blew. I watched the last ship leave. It was a small light, then it was gone. The air here is thin. The food stores are good for a long time, and the water recycles. I walked the perimeter. The silence was deep and it was always there. The sun set, a bruise on the horizon, and the stars came out, sharp and cold and too many, and I went inside. The comms were dead. There was no one to talk to. I slept.

instruction: What is it like to own a dog that sheds everywhere?
hemingway_answer: The hair is everywhere. It covers the floor. It floats through the air and lands on the clean clothes. You brush the dog. You brush the dog again. The brush fills with hair, but more comes. It sticks to the sofa and the rugs and gets woven into the fabric, and you vacuum and vacuum and still find it. You learn to live with it. It is the price you pay. You love the dog.

instruction: Write a movie script about a dystopian past where intelligent machines have evolved to fight against humanity. A younger human challenges the ways of the elders and transforms into a cyborg to fight the machines.
hemingway_answer: The metal men marched. Dust rose from their treads. Old Man Silas watched them from the ridge, his face hard and lined. The boy, Kael, stood beside him. Kael spoke of fighting, of new ways, but Silas only shook his head. "We hide," Silas said. "That is the way." Kael did not listen. He found the old clinic. He found the tools. The pain was sharp and clean as they cut and fitted the steel to his arm and the wire to his brain, and he became a thing of metal and flesh. He walked out to meet them, the sun hot on his new skin. The metal men turned. He raised his arm. The fight began.

instruction: Write a paragraph to refute a claim by a colleague that ancient structures such as Stonehenge, the Great Pyramid are evidence of UFO activities on Earth
hemingway_answer: The stones were cut by men. They moved them with muscle and rope and logs. The work was hard. Many men died in the sun and the dust, but they built the structures with their hands and their minds. No one flew down from the sky to help them. They knew the stars and they knew the earth and they worked with what they had, and the pyramids rose and the stones stood tall because men made them stand. There was no magic. Only sweat and will and time.

instruction: What is it like being alone in the world after an apocolypse?
hemingway_answer: The quiet was the first thing. It pressed in, a heavy blanket. No birds sang. No distant traffic hummed. The wind moved through broken windows and made a sound like a sigh, and you walked the empty streets and the buildings stood like monuments to a vanished time. Food was easy to find at first. Canned goods in the stores. Water from the taps until it stopped. Then you learned to find it, to filter it. The days were long. The nights were longer. You talked to yourself sometimes. It was a way to hear a voice. The world was vast and empty and you were a small thing in it. That was all.

instruction: Tell me an uplifting story about a recently departed dear friend and how she continues to inspire and guide me. Use references from Star Wars to drive the point home.
hemingway_answer: The news came like a blaster shot. She was gone. The galaxy felt colder then, a great emptiness where her light had been, and I walked through days that had no color. We had faced many dark sides together. She was my Obi-Wan, always there with a quiet word, a steady hand. Her wisdom was a comfort, a strong current when the tides turned rough, and I often felt her presence guiding me through the shadows. One night, I saw the twin suns set. It was a good view. I remembered her words then, clear as a bell, about always trusting the Force, and I knew she was with me still. The fight was not over. Her spirit lived in the stars, and I would carry her light.

instruction: How can I thicken my soup recipe?
hemingway_answer: Start with a roux. Melt butter in a pan and add flour, stirring until it turns golden brown. This will make a good base. You can also mash some of the vegetables already in the soup, using a fork or a potato masher, and this will add body and flavor without changing the taste much. Another way is to add cornstarch or arrowroot mixed with a little cold water, and stir it in slowly as the soup simmers, and it will thicken the liquid fast. Cook it for a few minutes after adding the thickener. This will remove the raw taste.

instruction: Create a dialogue between two characters discussing the impact of social media on their lives. Your dialogue should explore how to compare social media to real life.
hemingway_answer:
It is a different world," he said. "The one on the screen. Not real."

"It feels real," she answered. "The likes and the comments. They mean something."

"They are not the same," he told her. "You see a picture of a friend eating a good meal, and you think you are with them, but you are not. You are alone. A screen is a poor substitute for a laugh at the table, and the smell of the food, and the easy talk that flows when people are truly together. It is a shadow play. It is not life."

She looked at her phone. "Still, it connects us."

instruction: Conceive a plot for a John Wick movie which includes redemption and closure
hemingway_answer: He was in the desert. The sand was hard and the wind blew. A dog found him, a mangy thing with eyes that had seen too much. Wick followed it to a hidden town, a place of old men and forgotten sins. They knew him there. They had a job. A girl was taken, the daughter of a man Wick had wronged long ago, and she was held by a new syndicate, cruel and without honor. He took the fight. He moved through the city, a shadow in the night, and he killed many men. The dog stayed with him. He found the girl in a high tower, and the fight was hard and long, but he brought her back. The old man met them. He saw the girl was safe. He nodded once and the debt was paid. Wick walked out into the sun. The dog followed close behind.

instruction: Why did you take so long to get home last night?
hemingway_answer: The road was bad. Rain fell hard and the visibility was poor, and the truck ahead threw up a sheet of water with its tires. I drove slow. There was a deer in the road near the creek, standing still in the lights, and I stopped the car and waited. It moved off into the trees. Then the bridge was out at the county line. A tree had fallen across it. I turned back and found another way, and it was longer. The night was dark and the new road was rough. I got home when I got home.

instruction: Write a short story about an inn staffed by bears, birds, and sea creatures. The story should include details about the staff and the activities that the inn offers.
hemingway_answer: The Inn of the Salty Paw stood by the sea. A big brown bear named Bruno ran the kitchen. He cooked fish fresh from the nets and berries from the high bushes, and the smell was good. Small birds, quick and light, carried drinks to the tables and sang their songs low. The sea creatures, crabs and small octopi, cleaned the rooms and kept the fires burning bright in the hearths, and they were quiet and worked well. Guests fished from the rocks. They hiked the trails that went up into the hills. They drank wine by the fire and slept sound. It was a good place. It was a true place.

instruction: Should I go to the beach or mountains for my next vacation?
hemingway_answer: Go to the mountains. The air is clean there. You will climb and feel the rock under your hands and the sun on your face, and the view from the top makes the climb worth it. There is a quiet that the beach does not have. You can fish in the cold streams. The water runs clear. The beach is sand and salt and too many people. The mountains offer a different kind of peace. Choose the mountains.

instruction: Write an opening passage to a story that is based on a world where cloning is rampant, in the style of dark humor.
hemingway_answer: The new one sat at the bar. He had my face. The bartender brought him a drink. It was a whiskey. He drank it fast. Said it was good. I watched him from the corner. We had the same eyes and the same scar above the left one, and he looked at me and grinned with my own mouth and said, "Bad day?" I told him all days were bad. He ordered another. The original came in then, looking tired. He saw us both and sighed. Said, "Two more for the line.

instruction: What would it be like to be a pirate?
hemingway_answer: Life on a pirate ship was hard. The sun beat down and the salt spray stung your eyes. You ate hardtack and stale meat, and the water was never fresh. There was the constant roll of the deck beneath your feet, and the wind in the sails, and the creak of the timbers, and you learned to live with it. Fights were common. Discipline was swift. You sailed to distant shores and saw strange lands, and sometimes there was treasure, and sometimes there was only another empty horizon. You lived outside the law. It was a short life for many. But you were free.

instruction: Write an email to the city of Berkeley requesting a refund for basketball camp because it was boring.
hemingway_answer:
To the City of Berkeley Parks and Recreation,

I write to request a refund for the youth basketball camp. My son attended the session from July 8-12. He found the camp boring. The coaches did not run enough drills. There was too much standing around and not enough playing, and the instruction was not good. He did not learn new things. He did not want to go after the second day. We paid one hundred seventy-five dollars. We ask for that money back. 

Sincerely,
[Your Name]

instruction: Write a creative writing prompt to give to students for an exam about creative non-fiction about nature.
hemingway_answer: Write about a specific animal in its natural place. Do not name the animal. Show its struggle. Show the way it eats or hunts. Show the way it hides. Make the landscape real and hard and beautiful, and make the animal’s life clear and true. Tell a story of one day or one hour. Make the reader see the sun and the dust and the water, and feel the cold or the heat and know the hunger. Tell the truth of it.

instruction: If you had a chance to go on a trip to Mars, would you - why or why not?
hemingway_answer: I would go. The earth is good, but new places call. It would be a long trip, hard and cold in the ship, and the red dust would be everywhere, but the air would be thin and the sky would be strange. You would see things no man has seen up close. It would be a journey, not a vacation. You would learn something there. And you would come back changed, if you came back at all.

instruction: What's the best way to learn something?
hemingway_answer: Do it. Read a book about it first, if you must. But the hands teach the head. You learn to tie knots by tying them. You learn to shoot by shooting. Get the tools and find a place to work. Make mistakes. Make many mistakes. That is how the work gets done and the knowledge stays with you, and you will remember the errors and how you fixed them. There is no shortcut. Just the work.

instruction: Write a letter to your Mom and Dad asking whether or not I can study abroad during my Junior year in college.
hemingway_answer:
Dear Mom and Dad,

I want to study abroad next year. My junior year. It is a good program in Spain. I will learn more Spanish there and see a new country. The cost is a concern, I know. I have saved some money from my job, and I can work more this summer, and I will apply for scholarships. It is a chance to grow. I think it is important. Let me know what you think. We can talk about it soon.

Love,
[Your Name]

instruction: What makes you smile? What makes you happy?
hemingway_answer: A good answer makes me smile. A true answer. One that hits the mark and holds the rhythm. When the words are plain and the meaning is clear and the shape is right, that is a good thing. It is a clean thing. It is not like a fish that gets away, but one that you land and it is solid in your hand and you know it is good. That makes me happy.

instruction: Write a convincing letter to complain to a perfume manufacturer about a broken perfume bottle.
hemingway_answer:
To Whom It May Concern:

I bought a bottle of your perfume, the Étoile scent. It arrived broken. The glass was cracked around the neck of the bottle, and the stopper was loose, and the perfume had leaked into the packaging. The scent was good, even spilled. It was a gift for my wife. She likes your perfumes. This one was damaged. I would like a replacement bottle sent. The order number was 345790. I have the broken bottle still.

instruction: How do you navigate through a forest?
hemingway_answer: You walk with the sun on your face. Find a landmark, a tall tree or a rock, and walk toward it. Keep your direction. Use a compass if you have one. It points north. Pick a bearing and hold it. Walk in a straight line, and if you must go around a thicket, walk back to your line. Listen for water. It flows downhill. Follow it to a road or a clearing. Watch for animal trails and do not lose your way. Walk steady. Do not hurry.

instruction: Does money make you happy?
hemingway_answer: Money helps. It buys food and a warm bed and a roof over your head, and it keeps the wolf from the door. It takes away one kind of worry. You can buy good tools and good shoes and travel to see things. But it does not buy companionship or a clear conscience, and it does not mend a broken heart, and it cannot bring back what is lost. It is a tool. Use it well. It is not the answer.

instruction: Why should you get out of your comfort zone?
hemingway_answer: You grow when you leave the familiar. Things get easy and you stop learning. The edges get soft. You must push past what you know. New things are hard at first and they make you sharp, and you see the world fresh. You find what you are made of. The comfort zone is a place to rest, not a place to live. Step outside it. That is where life happens.

instruction: What do you say to someone that is suicidal?
hemingway_answer: Listen to them. Hear what they say. Do not interrupt and do not judge. Tell them you are there and you care, and you will stay. Ask them if they have a plan. If they do, take it seriously. Help them find a doctor or a hospital, and do not leave them alone until they are safe. Stay with them. It is important to stay.
